resources.string: Put on the viewer, look straight ahead, then press any button or tap the screen to start.
No controller: look at an item and tap the screen; tap while looking away to close the menu; long-press to recenter.

Lens calibration: do it once when you change viewer or phone. Video calibration: only needed if this video was shot crooked. Recenter mode: use \'Horizontal only\' when sitting or standing, \'Full orientation\' when lying down; recenter after changing posture.
Subject or horizon not straight ahead: press \'Set forward\'. Horizon tilted: adjust \'Horizon\' until the video\'s horizon lines up with the red line.
Look at the spot in the video you want straight ahead (e.g. the subject), then press A or tap the screen.
Fine-tune forward. If your eyes tire after a while or near objects look doubled, adjust Eye vertical offset and Convergence.

Centering: close one eye at a time. The rings\' center should sit in the middle of the lens, and the lens edge should cut off the same amount of the yellow frame on all four sides. Center too far left: move \'Horizontal offset\' right; too low: move \'Vertical position\' up. If one eye is high and the other low (phone is tilted), adjust \'Tilt\'.

IPD: the left eye sees the top and left halves of the cross, the right eye the bottom and right halves. Adjust \'Lens separation\' until the two segments join into one straight line and the horizontal lines line up too; the yellow ring is a reference both eyes see.

Distortion: look straight ahead and adjust k1 until the middle lines are straight, then look at the edges and adjust k2. Finally turn your head left and right; the grid should look pinned to a wall. If it follows your head or slides the opposite way, adjust \'Screen to lens\'.
This phone has no head-tracking sensor; the view won\'t follow your head.
